ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.evidence: Develops academic writing and research-literacy skills alongside personal development and civic engagement. Students locate and evaluate scholarly sources, synthesize literature, formulate research questions and arguments, and construct a research-paper introduction. A community-engaged project with a societal partner connects these skills to collaboration, reflection and practical contribution. Personal development planning addresses learning goals, self-efficacy, and stress and time management; the course also considers responsible academic use of AI.
ACCPPDE101.topics: Scholarly sources and research questions; Argumentation and thesis statements; Literature synthesis; Academic integrity and referencing; Community engagement; Personal learning goals and reflective learning; Collaborative learning; Self-efficacy; Stress and time management; Responsible use of AI
ACCPPDE101.methods: Scholarly literature searching and source evaluation; Literature synthesis; CARS model for research introductions; Reflective development planning; Community project co-design
role: c4
Mandatory academic research literacy, reflective collaboration and professional development.

BENBUSI112.name: Accounting & Corporate Finance
BENBUSI112.evidence: Introduces financial accounting, management accounting and investment appraisal, including accounting's social role and accountability implications. Students record transactions, prepare and interpret financial statements, and analyze performance and financing. The course then examines costing, pricing, budgeting, organizational control and sustainable management accounting. Investment decisions are evaluated using accounting and discounted-cash-flow measures. A case study analyzes the misuse of an accounting principle and its financial-statement effects.
BENBUSI112.topics: Accounting and accountability; Financial reporting frameworks; Accrual accounting; Assets, liabilities and equity; Financial statements and cash flows; Accounting judgements and estimates; Costing and pricing; Budgeting and performance indicators; Organizational control; Sustainable management accounting; Investment appraisal; Accounting misuse
BENBUSI112.methods: Double-entry bookkeeping; Year-end accounting adjustments; Financial-statement preparation; Financial-ratio analysis; Variance analysis; Accounting rate of return and payback calculations; Net present value and internal rate of return; Cost-of-capital analysis; Accounting case analysis
role: c1
Costing, budgeting, reporting, performance and discounted investment appraisal directly support business accounting and finance.

BENBUSI211.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
BENBUSI211.evidence: Examines AI's business, economic and societal implications without requiring a technical background. AI foundations and limitations lead into applications across enterprise functions and industries, labour-market change, productivity, innovation, market structure and inequality. Governance, corporate responsibility, regulation and future scenarios connect technological developments to institutional choices. Students analyze business cases and competing scholarly arguments, then investigate a country's AI readiness, workforce, regulation and industrial policy.
BENBUSI211.topics: AI capabilities and limitations; AI in business functions and industries; Agentic AI; Market structure and business models; Automation and augmentation; Labour markets and productivity; Innovation and economic growth; Inequality; Techno-economic paradigms and economic narratives; AI ethics and societal impacts; Corporate governance and AI regulation; National AI readiness and industrial policy; Future AI scenarios
BENBUSI211.methods: Business-case analysis; Comparative analysis of economic arguments; Evidence-based policy argumentation; Comparative country AI-readiness analysis
role: a2
AI applications in firms, innovation, productivity, labour and corporate governance support organisational technology decisions, not programming competence.

BENBUSI311.name: Transnational Business Law
BENBUSI311.evidence: Studies legal frameworks governing cross-border business transactions, combining comparative and international perspectives with practical legal problem-solving. Topics include trade regulation, contracts and international sales, transport and documentary transactions, finance, services, intellectual property, foreign investment and digital commerce. Advisory assignments assess contractual outcomes, risk allocation, intellectual-property protection and e-commerce compliance. A simulated arbitration develops written legal argument and oral advocacy.
BENBUSI311.topics: International trade regulation; Comparative and international contract law; International sales; Transport of goods and Incoterms; Documentary transactions; International trade finance; Employment and sale of services; Intellectual-property protection; International commercial dispute resolution; Foreign direct investment; E-commerce and digital economy regulation
BENBUSI311.methods: Comparative legal analysis; Application of legal rules to commercial scenarios; Transport-risk allocation analysis; Intellectual-property strategy assessment; E-commerce legal-compliance analysis; Arbitration memorandum drafting and simulated advocacy
role: c3
Contracts, trade, transport transactions, intellectual property and e-commerce compliance supply concrete cross-border commercial-law content.

BENBUSI312.name: Money, Banking & Finance
BENBUSI312.evidence: Examines financial markets and institutions, including the pricing of bonds, stocks and derivatives, interest rates and their risk and term structure, commercial-bank balance sheets and performance, financial structure and regulation, banking fragility and financial crises, central banks, money creation and monetary policy. Students apply algebraic and graphical analysis to financial and monetary problems. In the Stanford Banking Game they manage a simulated bank, analyse performance in Excel dashboards, forecast financial statements, and make evidence-based decisions about loans, deposits, capital, liquidity and risk. A small research project extends a selected financial or monetary research article through additional literature, a case study or updated evidence.
BENBUSI312.topics: Financial markets and institutions; Bond, stock and derivative pricing; Interest-rate determination; Interest-rate risk and the term structure; Commercial-bank balance sheets and performance; Bank capital, liquidity and risk management; Financial structure and regulation; Banking fragility; Financial crises in advanced and emerging economies; Central banking; Money supply; Monetary-policy tools and conduct
BENBUSI312.methods: Algebraic and graphical financial analysis; Balance-sheet analysis; Duration gap analysis; Bank-management simulation (Stanford Banking Game); Excel-based financial dashboard construction and performance analysis; Financial-statement forecasting; Research-article extension using literature comparison, case study or updated data
role: c1
Financial markets, instruments, banking risk and a simulated bank provide financial-system analysis; not farm accounting or full corporate-finance equivalence.

BENECON111.name: Introduction to Economics
BENECON111.evidence: Introduces microeconomic principles and short-run macroeconomic analysis. The microeconomic component examines supply and demand, strategic interaction, consumer choice, production, costs and competitive markets. The macroeconomic component introduces output, unemployment and inflation, then relates goods and financial markets through the IS-LM model. Students use algebra and graphs to explain economic behaviour and apply models to economic issues.
BENECON111.topics: Supply and demand; Game theory; Rational consumer choice; Individual and market demand; Production and costs; Perfect competition; Aggregate output; Unemployment and inflation; Goods and financial markets; IS-LM model
BENECON111.methods: Algebraic and graphical economic analysis; Supply-and-demand analysis; Game-theoretic analysis; IS-LM modelling
role: c1
Production, costs, consumer choice, markets and algebraic/graphical economic analysis support business-economic reasoning.

BENECON211.name: International Macroeconomics
BENECON211.evidence: Examines short-, medium- and long-run macroeconomic dynamics and policy, including international dimensions. Students study goods, financial and labour markets, inflation and unemployment, economic growth, expectations and the open economy. IS-LM and IS-LM-PC models connect markets and policy effects. Algebraic and graphical analysis and interpretation of macroeconomic indicators support the evaluation of economic developments and fiscal and monetary policy.
BENECON211.topics: Goods and financial markets; Labour markets; Phillips curve; IS-LM and IS-LM-PC models; Economic growth; Saving and capital accumulation; Technological progress; Expectations; Open-economy macroeconomics; Fiscal and monetary policy; Business cycles and economic crises
BENECON211.methods: Algebraic and graphical macroeconomic analysis; IS-LM and IS-LM-PC modelling; Macroeconomic data and indicator analysis
role: c1
International macroeconomic markets, growth, expectations and policy provide a bounded external business-environment complement.

BENECON212.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
BENECON212.evidence: Develops microeconomic theory through consumer behaviour, imperfectly competitive markets and economy-wide allocation. Students examine choice under uncertainty, non-egoistic preferences and cognitive limitations, then monopoly, strategic behaviour and labour and capital markets. General equilibrium, efficiency, externalities and government complete the analysis. Algebraic problem-solving and graphical analysis are connected to the interpretation and evaluation of research papers.
BENECON212.topics: Choice under uncertainty; Non-egoistic preferences; Cognitive limitations; Monopoly; Imperfect competition and strategic behaviour; Labour markets; Capital markets; General equilibrium; Market efficiency; Externalities; Government intervention
BENECON212.methods: Algebraic microeconomic analysis; Graphical economic analysis; Critical evaluation of economic research
role: c1
Choice under uncertainty, strategic interaction, imperfect competition and allocation implement microeconomic and behavioural analysis.

BENECON311.name: Public Economics
BENECON311.evidence: Examines government intervention through the efficiency and equity effects of public policy. Market failure, public goods and externalities provide foundations for studying public production, collective choice, spending and taxation. Health, education, welfare and social insurance illustrate expenditure and redistribution questions. Students apply economic models, interpret data and graphs, evaluate research and develop a research proposal and paper.
BENECON311.topics: Role and size of government; Market efficiency and failure; Public goods; Externalities; Efficiency and equity; Public production; Public choice; Public expenditure; Health and education policy; Welfare programs; Social insurance; Taxation and redistribution
BENECON311.methods: Economic model-based policy analysis; Efficiency and equity assessment; Interpretation of economic data and graphs; Critical evaluation of public-economics research
role: a1
Externalities, efficiency/equity, taxation and evaluated policy evidence explain institutional conditions of responsible markets.

BENECON312.name: Econometrics
BENECON312.evidence: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.
role: c2
Description-supported OLS/GLS/IV, tests, Monte Carlo simulation and an empirical paper implement econometric evidence.

BENECON314.name: Behavioral Economics
BENECON314.evidence: This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions. Learn how actual behavior deviates from the predictions of traditional economic models due to biases, heuristics, and framing. Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.
role: a0
Description-supported biases, heuristics, framing and experiments supply behavioural-economic choice analysis.

BENENTR111.name: Consumer Product Design
BENENTR111.evidence: Teaches consumer-product design and development through projects that progress from understanding an existing product to creating a new one. Students investigate product mechanisms and environmental impact, interview potential customers, translate needs into specifications, select concepts, and develop production plans and prototypes where feasible. The final project integrates these stages with industrial scaling and elementary economic analysis. Sustainability, including material use, repairability, lifespan and circularity, informs design decisions throughout.
BENENTR111.topics: Consumer needs; Product concepts and specifications; Product working mechanisms; Prototyping; Laboratory-to-industrial production scaling; Materials and resource use; Product lifespan, repairability and circularity; Environmental impact; Production costs and commercial viability
BENENTR111.methods: Consumer interviews; Needs ranking and specification development; Concept-criteria matrices; Quantitative product modelling; Product investigation and experimentation; Prototyping; Process-flow diagrams and material balances; Environmental-impact estimation; Break-even analysis
role: a0
Customer interviews, specifications, concepts, prototypes, production plans and environmental effects directly develop consumer-oriented products.

BENENTR211.name: Marketing & Consumer Engagement
BENENTR211.evidence: Connects marketing strategy and consumer psychology to responsible brand development and customer engagement. Students study strategic planning, customer experience, qualitative and quantitative insights, brand identity, digital marketing and behavioural framing. Applied projects analyze a company's strategy and response to disruption, design a brand, and investigate a consumer phenomenon using academic literature and primary and secondary evidence. Customer-journey mapping translates findings into recommendations.
BENENTR211.topics: Strategic marketing planning; Marketing mix; Customer centricity and experience; Consumer journeys; Market research and augmented insights; Brand identity and image; Brand partnerships; Digital and social marketing; Responsible marketing; Consumer psychology; Nudging and framing; Emerging technologies and marketing agility
BENENTR211.methods: Marketing-strategy case analysis; Advertising-campaign analysis; Kapferer brand-identity prism; Brand design; Primary and secondary consumer research; Consumer-journey mapping; Disruption-response planning
role: a0
Consumer psychology, brand strategy, primary/secondary evidence and customer-journey analysis directly develop marketing and consumer engagement.

BENENTR212.name: Strategy & Digital Transformation
BENENTR212.evidence: The course explores how companies develop strategies and drive responsible digital transformation amid rapid technology change impacting the economy and society. Students develop a strategic plan, from vision to execution, and identify digital value opportunities. Using industry cases, they gain foresight into digital technologies and their impact on strategy, business models and social responsibilities.
role: c0
Description-supported strategic plans, digital opportunities, business models and responsible transformation implement business strategy.

BENENTR311.name: Market Research
BENENTR311.evidence: See how companies figure out what customers love and what they don’t. You’ll plan and carry out real research, analyze what you find, and share your results. Our course shows you how to gather opinions and turn them into smart business ideas. Ready to turn curiosity into career skills? Perfect for future marketers, analysts, or entrepreneurs.
role: c2
Description-supported planning and execution of customer research and reporting supply market evidence; no undocumented advanced methods invented.

BENENTR312.name: International Business & Governance
BENENTR312.evidence: Examines how international trade, globalization and political, sociocultural and technological forces shape firms' cross-border decisions. Economic foundations include trade theories, foreign direct investment, foreign exchange and the monetary system. Students analyze governance, responsibility and trade-policy conflicts, investigate an international-business question, and develop an evidence-based market-entry strategy covering country attractiveness and business functions. A tariff case applies game theory to stakeholder choices and negotiation.
BENENTR312.topics: Globalization; International trade theories; Foreign direct investment; Foreign exchange and international monetary systems; Trade policy and economic integration; Cross-border governance; Corporate responsibility; Sociocultural and technological business environments; International business strategy; Market entry; Marketing, supply chains and human resources; Economic warfare
BENENTR312.methods: Trade-policy case analysis; Game-theoretic stakeholder analysis; Secondary-data analysis and visualization; Country and market-attractiveness assessment; Market-entry strategy development; Research-question formulation and evidence evaluation
role: c3
Trade, foreign investment, governance, responsibility and researched market-entry strategies support international firm decisions.

BENGATE101.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
BENGATE101.evidence: Introduces entrepreneurship and core business functions through the development of a startup concept. Students use design thinking to discover customer needs, define a problem, generate and prototype solutions, and construct value propositions and business models. Marketing, finance, operations, human resources and funding inform a coherent business plan and investor pitch. Entrepreneurial cases and a startup simulation examine decision-making, early growth and business lifecycles, with attention to societal impact and sustainability.
BENGATE101.topics: Entrepreneurial mindset and pathways; Business environments, ownership and competition; Customer needs; Value propositions; Business models; Marketing and sales; Finance and accounting; Venture funding; Operations and human resources; Competitive positioning; Startup growth and business lifecycles; Sustainability and societal impact
BENGATE101.methods: Design thinking; Customer-needs discovery; Ideation and prototyping; Value Proposition Canvas; Business Model Canvas; Business planning; SWOT and risk assessment; Startup simulation
role: c0
Startup concepts, customer needs, business models, operations, finance and an investor pitch provide integrated business foundations.

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.evidence: Introduces empirical research design and statistical analysis, followed by a substantial student research project. Students study operationalization, measurement quality, sampling, surveys and experimental and nonexperimental designs, then descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression. R and R Commander support data display and analysis. Project teams develop instruments and a research plan, collect and analyze data, and report results under explicit research-ethics and privacy requirements.
BENGATE102.topics: Scientific inquiry and hypotheses; Operationalization and measurement; Reliability and validity; Survey construction and sampling; Randomized and quasi-experimental designs; Nonexperimental and qualitative research; Descriptive statistics; Sampling distributions and estimation; Hypothesis testing and confidence intervals; Association and regression; Research ethics and anonymous data collection
BENGATE102.methods: Survey design; Probability and nonprobability sampling; Experimental and nonexperimental research design; R and R Commander data analysis; Descriptive statistics and visualization; Scale-reliability analysis; One- and two-sample mean tests; ANOVA; Chi-square tests; Correlation and regression; Empirical data collection and analysis
role: c2
Research questions, measurement, sampling, designs, R statistics and an executed group study provide empirical methods.

BENLEAD111.name: Personal Leadership
BENLEAD111.evidence: Introduces leadership through self-leadership, leadership theory and emotional intelligence. Covey's habits provide a framework for personal vision, prioritization and collaboration, alongside transformational, authentic, situational and adaptive leadership perspectives. Students analyze personality and emotional-intelligence profiles in relation to group dynamics, examine leadership cases, and construct a personal development plan with actionable goals. Assessment tools support educational reflection rather than diagnosis, and the outline acknowledges differences in their scientific support.
BENLEAD111.topics: Self-leadership and self-awareness; Covey's seven habits; Emotional intelligence and emotion regulation; Personality and group dynamics; Transformational and authentic leadership; Situational and adaptive leadership; Evolutionary perspectives on leadership; Goal setting and prioritization; Conflict resolution and negotiation; Trust and collaboration
BENLEAD111.methods: Leadership theory and case analysis; Reflective personality and emotional-intelligence assessments; Eisenhower prioritization matrix; SMART goal setting; Leadership-development planning; Leadership simulations
role: Read as removed lead; more direct contributions strengthen the proposed concepts.

BENLEAD211.name: Psychology of Leading Under Pressure
BENLEAD211.evidence: Examines how emotion regulation, emotional intelligence, emotional expression and suppression, emotional labor, belonging, identity safety and psychological safety shape leadership and social interaction under conflict, exclusion and interpersonal uncertainty. It emphasises inclusive leadership and ethnic, cultural, sexual and gender minority experiences, with digital emotion regulation as a further strand. Students conduct a supervised quantitative survey project: formulating theory-driven hypotheses, selecting established psychological measures, designing and piloting a Qualtrics survey, recruiting participants ethically, collecting original data and preparing a clean dataset. Individual work applies descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlations, group comparisons and introductory multiple regression in SPSS or RStudio, and interprets findings and limitations in empirical reports and evidence-based leadership recommendations.
BENLEAD211.topics: Emotion regulation strategies; Emotional intelligence; Emotional expression and suppression; Emotional labor; Inclusive leadership; Belonging and identity safety; Psychological safety; Ethnic, cultural, sexual and gender minority experiences; Digital emotion regulation; Psychological measurement, reliability and validity; Ethical survey research in diverse populations; Interpretation and limitations of quantitative evidence; Evidence-based leadership recommendations
BENLEAD211.methods: Theory-driven hypothesis formulation; Quantitative survey research; Established psychological measure selection and evaluation; Qualtrics survey construction and piloting; Ethical participant recruitment and original data collection; Codebook development, reverse coding and scale scoring; Data cleaning and missing-data documentation; Descriptive statistics; Reliability analysis; Correlation analysis; Group comparisons; Introductory multiple regression in SPSS or RStudio; APA-style empirical reporting
role: c0
Emotional labour, inclusion and psychological safety support organisational leadership; an original survey builds workplace-research skills.

BENLEAD311.name: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
BENLEAD311.evidence: Examines organizational behaviour at individual, group and organizational levels. Topics connect personality, perception, emotions and motivation to teams, leadership, power, conflict, structure, culture and change. Students design research plans for organizational cases and conduct a brief systematic literature review using PRISMA reporting tools. Workshops develop literature searching, study selection, source appraisal and synthesis, linking organizational-psychology evidence to practical questions and recommendations.
BENLEAD311.topics: Diversity, equity and inclusion; Job attitudes and satisfaction; Emotions, stress and workplace health; Personality and individual differences; Perception and decision-making; Motivation; Group behaviour and work teams; Human resource systems; Communication, conflict and negotiation; Leadership, power and politics; Organizational structure; Organizational culture and change
BENLEAD311.methods: Organizational case analysis; Research design and hypothesis formulation; Systematic literature review; PRISMA flow diagrams and checklists; Database searching and study screening; Source-quality appraisal and evidence synthesis
role: c0
Motivation, teams, power, culture, structure, change and a systematic review directly support organisational behaviour.

BENLEAD312.name: Negotiation & Strategic Thinking
BENLEAD312.evidence: Develops negotiation as an analytical practice and interpersonal skill. Students learn interest-based bargaining, BATNA and ZOPA, value creation, framing, concessions and strategies for handling power, emotions and difficult counterparts. Social-psychological and communication perspectives connect negotiation to trust, ethics, culture and relationships. Frequent simulations and narrative analysis lead to an annotated negotiation film and the design, teaching and evaluation of a negotiation scenario grounded in Delta Climate Center themes.
BENLEAD312.topics: Interests versus positions; BATNA and ZOPA; Mutual gains and objective criteria; Dual-concern model; Anchoring, framing and concessions; Trade-offs and logrolling; Cognitive biases and influence; Power and emotions; Trust, reputation and ethics; Cross-cultural and organizational negotiation; Negotiation implementation and withdrawal; Stakeholder interests
BENLEAD312.methods: BATNA and ZOPA analysis; Stakeholder-interest mapping; Interest-based negotiation; Negotiation simulations; Narrative and film analysis of bargaining; Negotiation-scene scripting and annotation; Scenario design and reflective evaluation
role: c0
Bargaining, BATNA, value creation, power and simulations develop negotiation in stakeholder and business decisions.

DISARIN211.name: Decision-making in AI
DISARIN211.evidence: Develops the mathematical foundations of intelligent-agent decisions under uncertainty. Probability and Bayesian networks support belief updating and inference, while temporal models address changing environments. Decision theory, Markov decision processes, partial observability and bandit problems connect uncertainty to policies and expected utility. Multi-agent decisions introduce strategic and collective interaction, and probabilistic programming provides a framework for expressing models. Students work through equations, numerical examples and scientific papers.
DISARIN211.topics: Conditional probability, independence and Bayes' rule; Bayesian networks; Temporal probabilistic models; Hidden Markov models and dynamic Bayesian networks; Expected utility; Markov and partially observable decision processes; Exploration-exploitation trade-offs and bandits; Competitive and cooperative multi-agent interaction; Negotiation, auctions and voting; Probabilistic programming
DISARIN211.methods: Probabilistic inference; Bayesian-network modelling; Temporal probabilistic modelling; Expected-utility analysis; Sequential decision modelling; Game-theoretic analysis; Probabilistic programming
role: c1
Bayesian inference, expected utility, temporal models and sequential decisions complement deterministic business optimisation.

DISARIN311.name: Optimization Methods in AI
DISARIN311.evidence: Studies search and optimization for rational agents in known, complex and adversarial environments. Students move from uninformed and heuristic search to local and global optimization, first- and second-order methods and population approaches. Adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, linear programming and discrete optimization extend the toolkit. Laboratories and projects require algorithm tracing, implementation and evaluation and experimental investigation of small intelligent systems.
DISARIN311.topics: Intelligent and rational agents; Uninformed and informed search; Heuristic functions; Search in complex environments; Local and global optimization; First- and second-order optimization; Population methods; Adversarial games; Constraint satisfaction; Linear programming; Discrete optimization
DISARIN311.methods: Uninformed and heuristic search; Local and global search; First- and second-order optimization; Population-based optimization; Adversarial search; Monte Carlo tree search; Constraint-satisfaction algorithms; Linear programming; Discrete optimization; Algorithm implementation and experimental evaluation
role: c1
Constrained search, linear/discrete optimisation and evaluated implementations directly support quantitative decisions.

DISDATA111.name: Introduction to Data Science
DISDATA111.evidence: Introduces data analysis and visualization in R through practical work with tabular, textual and spatial data. Students import, clean, transform and join data, explore patterns, and construct visualizations using tidy-data principles and the grammar of graphics. Web scraping and basic programming functions extend the workflow. A student research project applies these tools to a question using data from a field of interest.
DISDATA111.topics: Data visualization; Exploratory data analysis; Tidy data; Data transformation and integration; Dates and times; Web data; Text data; Geospatial data; Programming functions; Data-based research questions
DISDATA111.methods: R programming; ggplot visualization and grammar of graphics; Data cleaning, tidying and transformation; Data import and joins; Web scraping; Text-data analysis; Geospatial-data analysis
role: c2
R importing, cleaning, joining, visualisation and a data project support market and organisational evidence workflows.

DISDATA211.name: Machine Learning
DISDATA211.evidence: Introduces statistical learning for understanding data and predicting outcomes. Students study regression and classification, model accuracy, resampling, regularization, nonlinear models, trees, support vector machines and unsupervised learning. Practical assignments evaluate methods on real data using R or Python. Projects emphasize informative predictor construction, test-set prediction, appropriate model choice and clear reporting of results and limitations.
DISDATA211.topics: Prediction and model accuracy; Regression and classification; Resampling and validation; Model selection and regularization; High-dimensional data; Nonlinear regression; Tree-based learning; Support vector methods; Dimension reduction; Unsupervised learning; Feature engineering
DISDATA211.methods: Linear and logistic regression; Generative classification; Cross-validation and bootstrap; Subset selection; Ridge regression and LASSO; Splines and generalized additive models; Basic and advanced decision-tree methods; Support vector machines; Principal component analysis; Clustering; Predictive-performance evaluation; R or Python implementation
role: a2
Regression, classification, validation and predictor evaluation support statistical market inquiry; no business dataset is guaranteed.

DISGATE101.name: Introduction to Programming
DISGATE101.evidence: Introduces computational problem-solving and programming in Python. Students develop structured programs using branching, iteration, functions and data collections, then progress to recursion, exception handling and object-oriented programming with inheritance. Elements of logic, sets and enumeration support computational reasoning. Exercises and projects require students to write, trace, test, debug and explain programs that solve problems of moderate complexity.
DISGATE101.topics: Python language fundamentals; Strings and input/output; Branching and loops; Functions; Tuples, lists, sets and dictionaries; Aliasing and cloning; Recursion; Exceptions and assertions; Object-oriented programming; Inheritance; Computational problem-solving
DISGATE101.methods: Structured programming in Python; Object-oriented programming; Recursive problem-solving; Program tracing; Testing and debugging; Exception handling
role: c2
Python programming, structured data, testing and computational problem solving support reproducible business-data methods.

DISGATE102.name: Mathematical Methods
DISGATE102.evidence: Develops single-variable calculus and related mathematical tools for modelling scientific problems. Functions, limits and differentiation lead to optimization, Taylor series, complex numbers, integration and differential equations. Students solve problems analytically and with Mathematica, including numerical approximation. A project implements, analyzes and adapts a dynamic model, requiring interpretation of its behaviour and explanation of the computational results.
DISGATE102.topics: Functions and limits; Continuity; Differentiation; Optimization; Taylor series; Complex numbers; Definite and indefinite integrals; Integration techniques; First-order differential equations; Population-growth and predator–prey models; Second-order linear differential equations; Dynamic models
DISGATE102.methods: Analytical differentiation and integration; Taylor approximation; Newton's method; Numerical integration; Euler's method; Analytical solution of differential equations; Computer algebra with Mathematica; Dynamic-model implementation and analysis
role: c1
Calculus, optimisation, differential equations and model implementation provide quantitative foundations, without claiming the complete vector/matrix curriculum.

DISMATH213.name: Computational & Numerical Methods
DISMATH213.evidence: Develops numerical solutions to mathematical problems that lack convenient analytical solutions, emphasizing when algorithms work and how to validate their output. Students study numerical root finding, interpolation, differentiation, quadrature, ordinary differential equations, and linear and nonlinear systems. Mathematica notebooks apply and compare textbook algorithms with built-in routines, with attention to roundoff, convergence, error, stability and sensitivity.
DISMATH213.topics: Computer arithmetic and roundoff; Algorithm convergence and error; Scalar root finding; Polynomial interpolation and splines; Parametric curves; Numerical differentiation and integration; Initial-value problems; Multistep and adaptive differential-equation methods; Stability and stiff equations; Linear systems and matrix factorization; Nonlinear systems; Numerical-result validation
DISMATH213.methods: Mathematica numerical computation; Bisection, fixed-point, Newton and secant methods; Polynomial and spline interpolation; Numerical differentiation and Richardson extrapolation; Simpson, Romberg and Gaussian quadrature; Adaptive quadrature; Euler and Runge-Kutta methods; Multistep predictor-corrector methods; Gaussian elimination and pivoting; Matrix factorizations; Newton and quasi-Newton methods for systems; Steepest descent; Continuation methods
role: Read as removed lead; more direct contributions strengthen the proposed concepts.

DISMATH314.name: Probability & Statistics
DISMATH314.evidence: Provides a rigorous introduction to probability and mathematical statistics, from probability spaces and random variables to multivariate distributions and statistical inference. Students study estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests and maximum-likelihood methods, followed by an introduction to Bayesian reasoning. Mathematica simulations verify analytical results. A substantial project implements and compares random-sampling algorithms, including inverse sampling, accept-reject sampling and Gibbs sampling.
DISMATH314.topics: Probability spaces and conditional probability; Random variables and expectation; Moment-generating functions; Discrete and continuous distributions; Multivariate and conditional distributions; Transformations and correlation; Sampling and order statistics; Confidence intervals and hypothesis tests; Estimation efficiency; Bayesian inference; Monte Carlo methods
DISMATH314.methods: Analytical probability calculation; Maximum-likelihood estimation and testing; Chi-square tests; Bootstrap; EM algorithm; Bayesian updating; Inverse-transform sampling; Accept-reject sampling; Gibbs sampling; Monte Carlo simulation in Mathematica
role: c2
Probability, inference, likelihood and sampling-algorithm analysis support uncertainty and statistical reasoning.

ENSDELT311.name: R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation
ENSDELT311.evidence: Studies resource circularity through solar-panel recycling, metal recovery from electronic waste, and soil remediation using plants and mycelium. Theory and extensive laboratory work connect material composition and separation technologies to resource yields, environmental consequences and recycling constraints. Students develop leaching protocols, analyze metal concentrations and recovery, cultivate fungal networks, and use microscopy to characterize materials and mycelium growth.
ENSDELT311.topics: Circular resource supply; Solar-cell and solar-panel recycling; Delamination and material separation; Electronic waste; Pyrometallurgy and hydrometallurgy; Precious-metal recovery; Plastic-recycling legislation; Phytoremediation; Mycoremediation; Mycelium-based soil amendments
ENSDELT311.methods: Solar-panel dismantling and physical separation; Chemical leaching; Experimental-protocol design; ICP metal analysis; Electrochemical recovery; Scanning electron microscopy and EDS; Mycelium cultivation and growth characterization; Recovery-yield and resource-potential calculations
role: Read as removed lead; more direct contributions strengthen the proposed concepts.

ENSDELT312.name: Governance of Sustainability
ENSDELT312.evidence: Analyzes sustainability as a problem of collective decision-making involving governments, markets and civil society. Concepts of institutions, power, participation, justice and problem complexity frame competing technological and systemic responses. Structured cases examine food, freshwater, energy and climate mitigation. Students apply governance frameworks to a Zeeland issue, consult relevant organizations or experts, and produce policy advice or an evaluation assessing effectiveness, feasibility and stakeholder interests.
ENSDELT312.topics: Institutions, actors and power; Collective action and common-pool resources; Governance modes and networks; Techno-optimism and ecological limits; Climate justice; Populism and environmental politics; Wicked and long-term problems; Public participation; Food, water and energy governance; Markets, public goods and externalities; Adaptive and global governance; Climate mitigation; Policy effectiveness and feasibility
ENSDELT312.methods: Governance-framework application; Problem diagnosis and causal analysis; Stakeholder and policy-option matrices; Policy evaluation; Policy-advice memo development; Stakeholder and expert interviewing; Comparative analysis of normative policy perspectives
role: a1
Institutions, markets, civil society, food/energy cases and policy advice support sustainability governance around firms and consumers.

ENSGATE101.name: Sustainability Essentials I
ENSGATE101.evidence: Uses planetary boundaries to introduce scientific tools for understanding sustainability and human impacts on Earth systems. Students interpret graphs and uncertainty, build simple dynamic models, and learn chemical, thermodynamic and mechanical principles relevant to environmental processes. Topics connect climate, ocean acidification, nutrient cycles, energy and materials. An iterative laboratory project makes starch-based biopolymers and measures their strength and elasticity to improve the formulation.

ENSGATE101.methods: Graph interpretation and comparison; Fermi estimation; Difference-equation and first-order linear differential-equation modelling; Elementary differentiation and integration; Biopolymer preparation; Strength and elasticity measurement; Iterative experimental improvement

Planetary boundaries, physical/chemical processes and material tests provide environmental understanding for product-impact claims.

ENSGATE201.name: Sustainability Essentials II
ENSGATE201.evidence: Connects wave physics, chemistry and materials science to sustainability questions. Students study wave behaviour and observation methods, chemical analysis, microscopic material structure and macroscopic stress and strain. Practical sessions include wave applications and chemistry laboratory work. Reflective inquiries and a final project critically assess sustainability campaigns, identify greenwashing and communicate evidence-based improvements to a public audience.

ENSGATE201.methods: Oscilloscope wave visualization; Optical-spectroscopy interpretation; Fourier wave analysis; Copper dissolution and chemical analysis; Laboratory logbook documentation; Stress-strain analysis; Mohr's-circle application; Evidence-based greenwashing case analysis; Public sustainability-communication design

ENSSUST111.name: Climate Change
ENSSUST111.evidence: Introduces climate-change science, societal impacts, and mitigation and adaptation. Students examine greenhouse gases, feedbacks, tipping points, ocean acidification and sea-level rise, then consequences for ecosystems, agriculture, transport, buildings and health. Climate justice, governance, communication and misinformation connect physical changes to social responses. Solution pathways include energy systems, carbon removal and climate-adaptive planning. Students interview a stakeholder and produce a short film, alongside reflection on their own role.
ENSSUST111.topics: Anthropogenic climate change; Greenhouse gases; Feedback loops and tipping points; Ocean acidification and sea-level rise; Biosphere impacts; Agriculture, transport and construction; Climate and health; Climate justice and governance; Paris Agreement; Renewable energy and sustainable heat; Carbon removal and geoengineering; Climate communication and misinformation; Climate anxiety; Mitigation and adaptation
ENSSUST111.methods: Stakeholder interviewing; Short-film production for climate communication; Source-credibility evaluation; What? So What? Now What? reflective model
role: a1
Climate science, production and transport impacts, mitigation and stakeholder inquiry provide evidence for business climate responses.

ENSSUST112.name: Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy
ENSSUST112.evidence: Develops life-cycle approaches to evaluating products, processes and services within a circular economy. Students examine environmental, social and health consequences from resource extraction to disposal or reuse, together with costs, revenues and management strategies. Three preliminary projects develop different parts or forms of life-cycle analysis, followed by a project that integrates the stages into a full product or process assessment.
ENSSUST112.topics: Circular economy; Product and process life cycles; Resource extraction and reuse; Environmental impacts; Social and health consequences; Life-cycle management strategies; Product-based and process-based assessment; Costs and revenues; Sustainable product and process planning
ENSSUST112.methods: Life-cycle assessment; Life-cycle management strategy analysis; Environmental-impact estimation; Cost and revenue analysis; Integrated product or process assessment
role: a1
Environmental/social/health impacts, costs and complete life-cycle assessment directly evaluate circular product and process choices.

GOSGATE102.name: Law, Society & Justice
GOSGATE102.evidence: Introduces law through legal, social and normative perspectives. Students compare major legal traditions and survey public and private law, including constitutional, criminal, international, human-rights, property, contract and tort law. The second part examines justice, social control and change, race and gender. Case briefs, legal interpretation, demand letters and mock trials apply legal reasoning; a family-law topic supports the design of a small socio-legal research proposal.

GOSPHIL212.name: Ethics
GOSPHIL212.evidence: Studies moral reasoning through historical and contemporary ethical theories and close philosophical reading. Utilitarianism, consequentialism, Kantian ethics, virtue ethics, contractarianism and feminist ethics lead into Nietzsche's genealogy, Murdoch's account of goodness and Nagel's treatments of value, perspective, death and meaning. Reflection and research essays require interpretation, argument evaluation and an independent position on ethical theory or a practical ethical problem.

GOSPHIL212.methods: Close philosophical text analysis; Reconstruction and critical evaluation of moral arguments; Comparison of ethical theories; Conceptual analysis; Independent philosophical argument development

GOSPOLI311.name: European Union Politics
GOSPOLI311.evidence: Studies EU institutions, political actors, integration and policymaking, linking formal rules to current political issues. Students analyze representation, legitimacy, interests, agenda setting, decision-making and implementation. A substantial empirical project examines European Parliament committee amendments, connecting MEP ideology and possible interest-group influence to amendment activity. Students develop a project plan, code amendments, assess salience and trace legislative processes.

GOSSOCI212.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
GOSSOCI212.evidence: Develops qualitative inquiry from research design and preparation through data collection, management, analysis and dissemination. Students examine methodological foundations, ethics, positionality and reflexivity alongside interviews, focus groups, ethnography, documentary and visual approaches. Coding, thematic interpretation and NVivo support analysis. Research teams formulate a question, collect and analyze qualitative evidence, and report their methodological decisions, findings and limitations in staged assignments.

GOSSOCI215.name: Social Movements & Environmental Justice
GOSSOCI215.evidence: Focuses on social movement theories and environmental justice. Uses case studies from the Environmental Justice Atlas and integrates perspectives such as feminism, anti‑colonialism, degrowth and environmental peacebuilding to encourage civic engagement.
role: a1
Description-supported environmental justice, social movements and case analysis explain contested transitions around firms and consumption.

HCBPSYC111.name: Social Psychology
HCBPSYC111.evidence: Introduces the scientific study of how thoughts, feelings and behaviour are shaped by other people and social situations. Social cognition, the self, influence and persuasion lead into group processes, prejudice, aggression, prosocial behaviour, attraction and close relationships. Students critically examine empirical research, synthesize findings from journal articles, formulate theory-guided questions and design a feasible study. The final project proposes research rather than conducting an empirical investigation.
HCBPSYC111.topics: Social cognition and person perception; The self and self-motives; Social influence; Persuasion, attitudes and behaviour; Group processes; Prejudice, stereotyping and discrimination; Prejudice reduction; Interpersonal aggression; Prosocial behaviour; Interpersonal attraction and close relationships
HCBPSYC111.methods: Critical appraisal of empirical social-psychology research; Literature synthesis; Theory-guided hypothesis formulation; Research design for a proposed social-psychology study

Social cognition, influence, persuasion, group processes and research appraisal supply actual psychological foundations for consumer behaviour.

MCCCOMM311.name: Persuasive Communication
MCCCOMM311.evidence: Examines contemporary persuasion through communication studies, social psychology and ethical analysis, then applies it in community-engaged work. Students study coactive persuasion, framing, argumentation, cognitive shortcuts and verbal and nonverbal communication. Projects with the Delta Climate Centre and Vlissingen municipality develop communication encouraging sustainable and circular lifestyles. An individual research paper evaluates selected persuasion tools through literature review, field research diaries and reflective analysis of their use.
MCCCOMM311.topics: Persuasion models and psychology; Ethics of persuasion; Coactive persuasion; Verbal and nonverbal communication; Message framing; Argumentation; Cognitive shortcuts and nudging; Science and sustainability communication; Circular lifestyles; Community-engaged communication

role: a0
Framing, persuasion and actual circular-lifestyle communication projects connect consumer influence to sustainable behaviour.

findings: The closest provisional response materially addresses business management, marketing, accounting, markets, organisational behaviour and empirical methods. Added actual optimisation and uncertain decisions, with mathematical foundations. Removed the title’s unsupported implication of dedicated supply-chain training. No programme-level equivalence or full food/sensory formation is claimed.
